content.text:
I've reorganized account settings into three places, each with one job. I couldn't check the signed-in Account page in a browser, because that needs a real Not Organic sign-in.

| Page | What it's for | What's on it |
|---|---|---|
| **My Desk** `/desk/` | What you've done | Writing activity, AI usage, costs. The export/sync/delete block is replaced by a link to Account. |
| **Account** `/account/` (new) | Who you are and what you own | Twyne address (alias), public profile, what your profile shares, Not Organic, your data, CLI & MCP tokens, delete account. Links at the top jump to each section. |
| **Preferences** `/settings/` | How the app behaves | Language, appearance, about the writer, interview style, AI providers, models, research. Nothing account-related is left on it. |

**New features:**
- **Profile links:** you can add up to 6 links (website, Bluesky, newsletter…) on your profile. They show under your bio on your public page. Only `https` addresses are accepted, a bare `example.com` gets `https://` added, and a blank label falls back to the domain name.
- **Not Organic achievements:** the Account page shows the achievements you've earned across all Not Organic apps, read from Not Organic's own records. The same section shows your email, account ID (DID), and links to your wallet and Not Organic account.

**Other fixes:**
- Preferences was titled "The Editor's Desk", which was easy to confuse with My Desk. It's now "Preferences" in all six languages; I wrote the non-English versions myself, so a native speaker should check them.
- The account menu now reads My Desk → Account → Preferences.

**How it's built:** the profile, token and delete-account code moved out of the 5,500-line `settings/index.tsx` into `src/components/account/`, which takes that file down to about 4,100 lines. Profile links are a new optional `links` field on the `handles` table. Achievements come from a new action, `providerIdentity.getAchievements`.

**Checks:**
- Types check clean in the changed files.
- The targeted tests pass, including a new test for the profile-link rules. I updated the source-wiring tests for the new file locations.
- In a headless browser, `/account/`, `/settings/` and `/desk/` load with no page errors, but Account only showed its signed-out screen.
- I didn't run the full test suite or e2e tests.
- `convex codegen` contacted the dev deployment, but I didn't run `convex dev` or deploy.

**Before you rely on it:**
- **Usage export is now all-time.** On My Desk it exported the selected date range; on Account it exports your whole history.
- **There's still no whole-account export.** "Your data" covers usage history only, and each piece is still exported from its own folio menu. An "export everything" option would need a new backend job — tell me if you want it.
- **Achievements depend on Not Organic.** The Not Organic code allows Twyne to read them, but I haven't confirmed the live service accepts that from Twyne. If it doesn't, the section shows "could not be loaded" instead of breaking the page.

# Achievements and referrals: operator and integration guide

Status: implemented and tested locally. This work has not deployed code, created
promotions, issued rewards or changed live PDS records. A read-only production
check on 2026-10-10 found that hosted OAuth metadata still advertises only
`atproto`, and the gateway has no Baste or Frenzy assertion key configured.

## Enabling an integration

1. Keep each product's private Ed25519 assertion key in that product's backend.
   Configure only its public JWK on the gateway as
   `<PRODUCT>_ASSERTION_PUBLIC_JWK`. Key loading now uses `PRODUCT_IDS`, including
   Baste and Frenzy, and rejects private keys, wrong curves and invalid key use.
   The original four required keys remain required; missing optional products
   remain disabled without interrupting the others. Railway `preserve()` entries
   retain provisioned keys; they do not generate or install new credentials.
2. Deploy the Convex achievement/referral schema and functions before the
   gateway and portal that call them. Deploy the landing service's identity
   frontend as well: it serves the account UI on `id.notorganic.info`.
   The portal Dockerfile includes the shared `convex/publicProfile.ts` helper.
   The landing Dockerfile includes the portal's shared login, access and admin
   browser contracts. All three images build locally with the pinned Bun version.
3. Verify hosted client metadata advertises `transition:email`,
   `repo:info.notorganic.achievement` and `blob:image/png` in addition to
   `atproto`. Ordinary sign-in still requests only `atproto`; publishing is an
   explicit additional authorization. Deploying metadata alone grants no user
   permissions and does not upgrade existing sessions.
4. Run `rtk proxy bun scripts/check-account-integrations.ts --public-only` to
   check the hosted metadata. In an environment containing the gateway's public
   keys, omit `--public-only` and add `--require-product frenzy` (or `baste`) to
   check that integration. The command prints product names and validation
   failures, never key values. This narrow check does not establish a matching
   backend private key, deployed Convex functions or a real OAuth round trip.
5. Configure an achievement/referral policy below, then verify an authorized
   account flow, explicit publishing consent and public record/receipt before
   calling the integration live. Use zero rewards for non-promotional checks.

On 2026-10-10 Railway has no Frenzy service, and its Baste service has no
assertion-key variables. A backend destination is needed before those private
keys can be installed. Do not share another product's signing key to bypass this.

## Authority

- The Convex ledger (`convex/achievements.ts`, `convex/referrals.ts`) is the only
  authority for awards, claims and rewards. A PDS record (`info.notorganic.achievement`)
  is a display copy the owner can edit; never infer an award or reward from it.
- Writes come only from an application's server through the gateway with a
  service token. The DID is the token subject; the application is the token
  product. Request bodies never carry a DID.
- Credit is issued through the wallet grant path in the same transaction as the
  award or qualification, with deterministic keys (`achievement:<awardId>`,
  `referral:<claimId>:referrer|referee`). Retries replay; they never pay twice.

## Setting up (administrators)

Portal → Admin → **Achievements and referrals**. The panel only renders for
accounts with admin access. The portal checks session, CSRF and admin access on
`/api/admin/*`; Convex re-checks the `NOTORGANIC_ADMIN_DIDS` allowlist and writes
every change to the admin audit log.

- **Achievement**: application, key (`first-lesson`), title, description, image
  path (a PNG under `/achievements/` or `/brand/` served by the portal), optional
  credit. Credit is blank (zero) by default. Only set it for an approved promotion.
  Turning an achievement off stops new awards; already-issued awards keep the
  title, description and image they were issued with.
- **Referral policy**: application, the event name the application will report
  (for example `first_purchase`), referrer and new-member credit (both zero by
  default). Without an active policy, no referral qualifies or pays.

API equivalents: `GET|PUT /api/admin/achievements`, `PUT /api/admin/referral-policies`.

### Starter catalog

`unison/src/achievement-catalog.u` defines 48 starter achievements, six for each
registered application (Not Organic, Keating, Twyne, Interleave, Stich, Voxq,
Baste, Frenzy). On the native account pages, **Admin → Starter catalog → Install**
adds every entry that is missing. Each one goes through the same audited
`PUT /api/admin/achievements` route as a hand edit, with zero credit. Entries that
already exist, including ones an operator changed, are skipped. If a definition
is refused, installation stops there; running it again continues from that point.

Installing a definition only makes it awardable. Nothing is awarded until an
application's backend calls `POST /v1/achievements/awards` with that key. Wiring
those calls into each product is still to do.

Tier (Seed, Sprout, Bloom, Evergreen), points, growth levels, hints and hidden
achievements are presentation only. They come from the catalog module, never
enter the ledger, and award no credit. A hidden achievement shows its hint until
it is earned. Badge art lives at `apps/portal/public/achievements/<app>/<key>.png`
and is generated by `rtk proxy bun scripts/achievement-art.ts` (needs ImageMagick
with librsvg). Regenerate it after adding catalog entries.

### Celebrations

When the account pages show an award this browser has not celebrated yet, they
play an unlock animation: the badge spins in with a WebGL foil, each
application has its own background shader, and points count up. Awards from the
last 21 days are celebrated; older ones are marked as seen without one, so a new
device does not replay a whole history. Seen award IDs are kept in this
browser's `localStorage` and nowhere else. With reduced motion, the card still
appears but nothing moves, and no WebGL runs. Without JavaScript, nothing is
celebrated, and the collection, filters and every action still work.

## Rules the ledger enforces

Achievements
- An application issues only its own achievements. Inactive definitions cannot be
  awarded, but a retry of an award that already succeeded replays.
- No award to a deleted account (account `deletedAt` or a provider deletion
  request), a locked/recovering account, or a suspended/deleted app mapping.

Referrals
- A click on `/r/<code>` only redirects with `?ref=<code>`; it records nothing.
- A claim is recorded by the application's server after sign-in. Rejected: self
  referral, a second referrer for the same account and app, accounts that joined
  the app before the code existed, revoked codes, codes whose owner is deleted or
  inactive.
- Frenzy may record claims for other applications (cross-app viral loops), but
  its assertion does not prove membership in the target app, so the referee must
  already have an active mapping for that app.

## Setting up (administrators)

Portal → Admin → **Achievements and referrals**. The panel only renders for
accounts with admin access. The portal checks session, CSRF and admin access on
`/api/admin/*`; Convex re-checks the `NOTORGANIC_ADMIN_DIDS` allowlist and writes
every change to the admin audit log.

- **Achievement**: application, key (`first-lesson`), title, description, image
  path (a PNG under `/achievements/` or `/brand/` served by the portal), optional
  credit. Credit is blank (zero) by default. Only set it for an approved promotion.
  Turning an achievement off stops new awards; already-issued awards keep the
  title, description and image they were issued with.
- **Referral policy**: application, the event name the application will report
  (for example `first_purchase`), referrer and new-member credit (both zero by
  default). Without an active policy, no referral qualifies or pays.

# Deploying Twyne

Twyne ships as a Qwik City SSR app. The browser bundle is built by Vite into
`dist/`, the SSR server entry into `server/`, and `server.js` (Node `http`)
serves both and listens on `$PORT`.

## Railway (primary)

The repo is configured for [Railway](https://railway.com) via `railway.json`
(`builder: RAILPACK`) and [`railpack.json`](https://railpack.com) — Railpack is
Railway's successor to Nixpacks:

- **Install** (Bun): `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- **Build** (Bun): `bash scripts/railway-build.sh` — runs Convex deploy + Vite
  client + Vite SSR server. If `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is unset, the script
  degrades to a frontend-only build (backend left untouched).
- **Start** (Node): `node server.js`
- **Healthcheck**: `GET /`

> The `build` step is auto-generated by Railpack from the Node provider
> (uses the mise step to install `bun` + `node`, then runs
> `bun install --frozen-lockfile`). We only override the `build` step to
> inject the Convex deploy + Vite build via `scripts/railway-build.sh` —
> the script is required because the inline `if/then/else` with nested
> single-quoted `&&` strings gets mangled by the build step's shell
> serialization.

`railpack.json` pins `node: 20` + `bun: 1` so the runtime image has `node`
available for the start command (`server.js` uses `node:http`), while Bun does
the install and Vite build.

### One-time setup

1. **Create / link the service** (already linked to `Diogenesoftoronto/twyne`):

   ```bash
   railway add --service twyne --repo Diogenesoftoronto/twyne
   ```

   Railway auto-deploys on every push to the connected branch.

2. **Set environment variables** (see `.env.example` for the full list). The
   `VITE_*` values are baked in at build time, so they must be set on the
   service before the first build:

{
  "$schema": "https://railway.com/railway.schema.json",
  "build": {
    "builder": "RAILPACK"
  },
  "deploy": {
    "startCommand": "node server.js",
    "healthcheckPath": "/",
    "healthcheckTimeout": 120,
    "restartPolicyType": "ON_FAILURE",
    "restartPolicyMaxRetries": 5
  }
}
